I tried this code: ```rust #![crate_type="bin"] fn main(){ let has_argument = std::env::args().find(|x| x == "some-argument").is_some(); println!("Has argument: {}", has_argument); } ``` Compiled using this command: ``` rustc test_cmd.rs --edition=2021 -Zsanitizer=memory ``` I expected to see this happen: Compiled program runs successfully. Instead, this happened: Memory sanitizer detects read of unitialized memory. If I remove iteration over args, everything is OK. ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.77.0-nightly (3cdd004e5 2023-12-29) binary: rustc commit-hash: 3cdd004e55c869faa2b7b25efd3becf50346e7d6 commit-date: 2023-12-29 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.77.0-nightly LLVM version: 17.0.6 ```
